captured_turns.narration:
You look around the tavern carefully, but the scene does not change.

By the **fireplace**, Aulus shifts his weight and keeps his eyes on the room while the other guards trade idle words. He holds a cup and makes a slow scan of the room, with no trouble yet.

Bassus shifts his weight beside the loose knot of guards, glances past the fireplace toward the room’s exits, and takes a measured sip of wine. He says, “Keep your eyes open—nothing good comes from staring at the fire.”

Cato scans the half-empty room from the knot by the fireplace, then shifts his stance to keep sight of the door and the bar while the others share their wine.

I scan the half-empty room from the knot by the fireplace, then shift my stance to keep sight of the door and the bar while the others share their wine. *Eyes the hearthlight, then the street-facing entrance.*

captured_turns.narration:
You punch at Aulus, but his guard comes up. Your fist hits his forearm instead of his face, and he shoves you off balance with a hard step.

Aulus keeps his eyes on you and snaps his short sword free halfway. “Don’t do that again.”

He steps in hard, grabs your sleeve, and wrenches you back from the knot of guards. “Enough—hands off! You start fights here again, and I’ll have you bound.”

Bassus catches your forearm to pin your movement and angles his body between you and the other guards. “Back off. One more swing and I’m calling for the watch and you’ll be on the ground—no talk.”

Cato cuts in from the side of the fireplace knot, palm out to stop you, then slides his short sword free and points it at your chest. “Enough. We don’t settle fists in this tavern—back up, or I’ll make you.”

dialogue.response: You swing—my guard comes up. Your fist meets my forearm; I ride the impact, then shove you off balance with a hard step and snap my short sword free halfway, eyes locked on you. Don’t do that again.

npc_turns.action: I step in hard, wine cup jolting in my grip as I grab your sleeve and wrench you back from the knot of guards. “Enough—hands off!” My short sword clears a finger’s breadth, point angled low, eyes up on yours. “You start fights here again, and I’ll have you bound.”

Bassus’s hand shoots to your forearm, not to strike—just to pin your movement—while I angle my body between you and the other guards. “Back off. One more swing and I’m calling for the watch and you’ll be on the ground—no talk.”

I cut in from the side of the fireplace knot, palm out to stop you—then my short sword slides free with a quick, controlled motion, point hovering at your chest. “Enough. We don’t settle fists in this tavern—back up, or I’ll make you.”
